objective: Names are a countable set with no letters; a state gives each pair of names a neighbour distinction n(u, v) and each name a value; a uniform law treats all names alike. To be proved: (T1) every finitary law that allows a state allows one in which adjacency and values are constant (all names pairwise neighbours, or none; with identity distinctions also all names one place), so no finitary law forces a neighbour, bounded degree needs a forbidden homogeneous star, and no finitary law forces a finite board other than one place; (T2) with existence clauses giving every place exactly 2k neighbours, every board is a disjoint union of Schreier graphs of F_k, so the letters draw the degree and connectivity and their labelling comes free; (T3) a count law (a place's value and the multiset of its neighbours' values, with existence clauses for the degree) allows the universal cover of every component of an allowed board, so if it allows a board with a cycle it allows a tree; (T4) no first-order law forces connected boards when one of its boards has a component of infinite diameter, and a named square with coordinates mod 3 and an aperiodic tile set makes every component a plane; (T5) in a count law, two disjoint edges with the same pair of values can exchange partners and two far places of different value can exchange names, so every neighbour distinction and value is flipped by a finite change, against BOARD-DIST-20261110-001's frozen boards.
title: Boards of abstract names
